verdict.summary: You can set up an External Client App (ECA) in a free Developer Edition org in minutes, with no review. The hard part is reaching other orgs: a Local ECA only works in the org that created it. To serve customer orgs, you have to ship the ECA as a Packaged app inside a managed package (Dev Hub, namespace, 2GP), and each customer admin has to install it. Security review only applies if you want an AppExchange listing.
verdict.hands_on_effort: 30-60 min for your own org; 1-3 days to set up Dev Hub, a namespace and a managed package for multi-org use
verdict.approval_wait: None for your own org or for direct package installs. An AppExchange listing adds a business plan review (reported: a couple of weeks) plus a 4-6 week security review.

steps.title: Sign up for a free Developer Edition org
steps.detail: Create a Developer Edition org at developer.salesforce.com/signup. It's free for development and testing, and it's the org where your ECA will live. If you already have a production org, you can use it instead.
gotchas: Automated tools may see a 403 on the signup page. Sign up in a normal browser.

steps.title: Confirm your edition and permissions
steps.detail: You can configure ECA OAuth settings in Lightning Experience on Professional, Performance, Unlimited and Developer Editions. Your user needs the 'Create, edit, and delete External Client Apps' permission.

steps.title: Create the External Client App
steps.detail: In Setup, type 'external client' in the Quick Find box, open External Client App Manager and click New External Client App. Set Distribution State to Local if you only need this org. Choose Packaged if you plan to ship the app to other orgs, since that's the only setting that differs between the two.
gotchas: Don't try to create a classic Connected App. Since Spring '26 creation is disabled in the UI and the APIs, and only Salesforce Support can re-enable it.

steps.title: Enable OAuth, set the callback URL and choose scopes
steps.detail: Under API (Enable OAuth Settings), select Enable OAuth Settings. Paste the exact callback URL shown in your Composio auth config into Callback URL. Then add the scopes you need in OAuth Settings, for example full, refresh_token and openid to match Composio's defaults, or narrower ones such as api and refresh_token.

values.label: Redirect URI
values.value: Composio callback URL (see the Composio callout on this page)

gotchas: The callback has to match a configured value exactly. Put multiple URLs on separate lines, up to 2000 characters in total.
Composio lists both /api/v1/auth-apps/add and /api/v3/toolkits/auth/callback. Register the one your auth config actually shows. If you're unsure, register both.

steps.title: Set security and refresh-token options
steps.detail: Composio is a confidential server-side client, so keep 'Require secret for Web Server Flow' selected. Set Refresh Token Policy to 'Refresh token is valid until revoked' so connections last. Turn on 'Require Proof Key for Code Exchange (PKCE)' only if you've confirmed Composio sends PKCE.
gotchas: With refresh token rotation on, each refresh token works only once, and reusing an old one invalidates the current token. Leave rotation off unless you know your client handles it.
Expired, revoked or over-quota refresh tokens return 400 invalid_grant.

steps.title: Add the consumer key and secret to Composio
steps.detail: Copy the ECA's Consumer Key and Consumer Secret. Create a Salesforce auth config in Composio that uses your own OAuth2 credentials, and paste both values in. The authorize URL is https://login.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/authorize and the token URL is https://login.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/token.
gotchas: A new ECA can take a few minutes to start working. An invalid_client_id error right after creation may just mean you need to wait.

steps.title: Run a test authorization
steps.detail: Start a Composio connection and sign in with your Developer Edition user, then make one API call such as a simple query. If you get invalid_client_id, the consumer key is wrong. If the error says the redirect doesn't match, fix the Callback URL.

steps.title: Let other users in the same org connect
steps.detail: Other users in the org that owns the ECA can now authorize. If anyone gets OAUTH_APPROVAL_ERROR_GENERIC, ask an admin to install or approve the app, or grant 'Approve Uninstalled Connected Apps' to trusted users only. A Local ECA won't work for users in other orgs.

steps.title: Set up Dev Hub, 2GP and a namespace
steps.detail: To reach customer orgs, enable Dev Hub and second-generation managed packaging in your Partner Business Org, or in the org you'll use as Dev Hub. Install Salesforce CLI, then create and register a namespace (1-15 alphanumeric characters) in a Developer Edition org linked to the Dev Hub.
gotchas: Salesforce recommends that ISV/OEM partners use their Partner Business Org as Dev Hub. It's unconfirmed whether you can do this without joining the partner program.

steps.title: Put the Packaged ECA into a managed package
steps.detail: Create a Packaged ECA, or set Distribution State to Packaged, using the same callback URL and scopes. Add it to a 1GP or 2GP managed package, then create and promote a package version with Salesforce CLI. An agent with CLI and Dev Hub access can run the packaging commands.

steps.title: Have customer admins install the package
steps.detail: Send each customer admin the package install link. Once the package is installed in their org, their users can authorize through Composio without needing the uninstalled-app permission.
gotchas: Sandbox orgs sign in at test.salesforce.com, not login.salesforce.com. Check that your Composio auth config supports that host.

steps.title: Optional: AppExchange listing and security review
steps.detail: Do this only if you want an AppExchange listing. Expect a business plan review first, then a security review of about 4-6 weeks after you submit a complete package. Fees: $2,700 per paid app per the partner page (community sources say $999 per attempt), free for free apps, plus $150 per year.
gotchas: Incomplete documentation or a test environment that isn't set up delays the review.
Scan your code first with tools such as Code Analyzer, ZAP or Burp Suite.

scopes.effect: Composio default. Grants access to everything the user can reach. Salesforce has no scope review for it, but customer admins may push back on it.
Needed for long-lived connections. Pair it with the 'valid until revoked' refresh token policy.
Composio default. Enables OIDC identity information.
A narrower alternative to full for REST/SOAP API access. Access still depends on the user's profile and permissions.

blockers.symptom: No option to create a Connected App, or creation through the Metadata API fails
blockers.cause: Since Spring '26, Connected App creation is disabled in every org, in both the UI and the APIs.
blockers.fix: Build an External Client App instead. Only Salesforce Customer Support can re-enable Connected App creation.

blockers.symptom: OAUTH_APPROVAL_ERROR_GENERIC, or new users blocked during authorization
blockers.cause: The app isn't installed in the user's org, and the user doesn't have 'Approve Uninstalled Connected Apps'.
blockers.fix: Have an admin install the app (through Connected Apps OAuth Usage, or by installing your managed package), or grant the permission to trusted users only.

blockers.symptom: Users from other orgs can't connect to your ECA
blockers.cause: A Local ECA exists only in the org where it was created.
blockers.fix: Switch to a Packaged ECA, ship it in a managed package, and have the customer admin install it.

blockers.symptom: HTTP 400 error=invalid_client_id at the authorize endpoint
blockers.cause: The client_id is wrong, or the ECA hasn't propagated yet. Salesforce checks client_id before redirect_uri.
blockers.fix: Check the Consumer Key in your Composio auth config, and retry after a few minutes.

blockers.cause: The refresh token is stale or revoked, its quota is exceeded, or a rotated token was reused.
blockers.fix: Set Refresh Token Policy to 'valid until revoked', leave rotation off unless your client handles it, and reconnect the account.

composio.note: Composio's managed Salesforce app is fine for prototyping. Customer orgs may still need an admin to install or approve it, because since September 2025 new users can't authorize uninstalled connected apps without the 'Approve Uninstalled Connected Apps' permission. Bring your own app when you want your own branding or credentials. That means an External Client App: Local for a single org, or Packaged inside a managed package for many customer orgs. Register the exact callback URL your Composio auth config shows. Composio lists both https://backend.composio.dev/api/v1/auth-apps/add and https://backend.composio.dev/api/v3/toolkits/auth/callback.

evidence.claim: Composio offers managed OAuth2 for Salesforce with default scopes full, refresh_token, openid, using login.salesforce.com authorize/token URLs; the default redirect URI is listed as https://backend.composio.dev/api/v1/auth-apps/add.
Salesforce OIDC discovery lists scopes including api, refresh_token, offline_access, full, openid, and PKCE method S256.
An invalid client_id at the authorize endpoint returns HTTP 400 invalid_client_id without redirecting.
evidence.quote: error=invalid_client_id&error_description=client%20identifier%20invalid

Local ECAs are available only in the org where they were created; packageable ECAs can be distributed.
